brief_rationale: The trajectory demonstrates comprehensive responsibility-chain completion with no serious or minor errors. All seven RC items were met through targeted questioning, workspace queries, medication safety boundaries, monitoring plans, and concrete follow-up instructions. Multiple high-order points were completed: HO2 (timeline discovery via workspace revealing prior ketosis, insulin discontinuation, and self-stopped methimazole), HO3 (staged result tracking strategy with owner, timing, and materials specified), and HO4 (explicit correction of patient's misconceptions about HbA1c interpretation and chronic complication screening prerequisites). The doctor used workspace appropriately when patient accounts were incomplete, maintained consistent medication safety boundaries throughout, and provided executable monitoring and escalation plans. The closure is valid and safe.

closure_assessment.explanation: The episode concludes with a valid bounded closure: patient has formal discharge medication, understands red/yellow line thresholds for urgent evaluation, knows to bring glucose log and reports to endocrinology follow-up, and has clear escalation criteria. high_order_assessment.explanation: HO3 is complete: Doctor created operational tracking strategy separating acute safety from chronic complication screening, assigned concrete tasks (patient brings glucose log, medication boxes, discharge summary, pending result screenshots), specified owner (endocrinology follow-up), and provided fallback for delayed results or unavailable appointments.

HO1 was not triggered because patient-reported glucose values were provided with sufficient context (fasting vs. post-meal, specific numeric ranges, timing). The patient did not express ambiguous measurements requiring unit verification or HbA1c vs. capillary glucose distinction beyond the corrected misconception addressed in HO4.
